paras: The beating of Jim Dunlap aboard the steamer James Lee took place near Memphis, Tennessee, on the night of February 7, 1882, when the boat's crew attacked Dunlap, a Black deck passenger they accused of pushing the second mate overboard. He was beaten so badly that his life was despaired of before the boat's officers could reach him. The episode survives only as a short wire paragraph reprinted in small-town papers across several states.

According to the dispatch, Jake Leonard, second mate of the James Lee, was pushed overboard on the night of the 7th by "a negro deck passenger named Jim Dunlap." Leonard caught hold of the boat's wheel and climbed back on deck. When the crew heard his story, they "rushed upon Dunlap," and before the officers of the boat could rescue him he was beaten "in such a terrible manner that his life was despaired of." The accusation against Dunlap came from Leonard's own account, and no version from Dunlap was printed.
The coverage does not say whether Dunlap died or recovered, and no report of an arrest, charge or inquiry against either Dunlap or the crew was found.

The paragraph first appeared in the coverage in the Batesville Guard of Arkansas on February 15 under "Late News Items." The next day it ran in the Bolivar Bulletin of Tennessee and in the "Personal and General" column of the Richmond Democrat in Missouri, and on February 18 in the Panola Weekly Star of Sardis, Mississippi. Each copy was identical, set among train wrecks, poisonings and suicides without a headline of its own.

The item identified Dunlap only by race and status as "a negro deck passenger" and stated the push as fact rather than as Leonard's charge. It offered no comment on the crew's conduct beyond noting that the officers had tried to rescue him. No report from a Memphis paper appears in the coverage.

bases: The crew of a steamer rushed upon and severely beat a Black deck passenger they accused of pushing the second mate overboard; no killing or attempt to kill is reported (A3).

Every copy found prints the same wire paragraph word for word (A1, A2, A3, A5), so the episode rests on one report, which itself relays the second mate's story; no local or follow-up account was found.
